function: Learns the BS analog beamformer and the RIS reflection beam codebook (quantized phase shifts), with user clustering, to maximize beamforming gain and cut training overhead, pp. 3, 9-10.
system: RIS-aided mmWave MISO: BS with 32-antenna UPA and 4-bit analog phase shifters, passive reflecting RIS of 256 elements, single-antenna UEs, 60 GHz, pp. 3, 13.
method: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning: TD3 with Wolpertinger discretization, k-means user clustering, cascaded sub-array agents; bi-level reward from received power, no CSI, pp. 2-3, 6-10.
data_channel: DeepMIMO ray-tracing outdoor scenario O1_60 at 60 GHz: 16,000 users from rows 1201-1400, 5 multipaths; same scenario for learning and evaluation, p. 13.
test_conditions: Codebooks learned and evaluated on the same DeepMIMO scenario; sweeps over codebook size and RIS size (32, 256); unseen-user reuse is only asserted, not tested, pp. 13-14.
baselines: Non-learned: DFT, 4x and 16x oversampled DFT, multi-directional DFT [8] (overhead only), SVD upper bound. Learned: DDPG-based MA-DRL (convergence only, Fig. 6), pp. 13-14.
metrics: Beamforming gain, achievable rate (bps/Hz) and its CDF, beam training overhead in time slots, convergence iterations, pp. 13-15.
complexity: none; only beam training overhead in time slots (Table I) and qualitative low-complexity claims; no order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the DRL, pp. 14-15.
openness: No own code or link; uses the public DeepMIMO dataset [28], scenario O1_60, pp. 3, 13.
q1_support: p. 13: "from the DeepMIMO dataset [28]", outdoor scenario O1_60 at 60 GHz, used to build the cascaded channels for learning and evaluation. DeepMIMO ray tracing is a listed standard source.
q2_support: p. 14: "after the codebook has been learned, learning will not be repeated" for an unseen user, but this is only asserted. p. 13: all learning and evaluation use the single DeepMIMO scenario O1_60; no experiment tests another scenario, band or site.
q3_support: p. 13: "converges faster than the DDPG DRL method"; Fig. 6 plots beamforming gain against iterations, so the learned comparison concerns convergence, and the DDPG variant is the same MA-DRL framework with DDPG instead of TD3. Rate results (Figs. 7-9) compare only with DFT, oversampled DFT and SVD, which are non-learned.
q4_support: p. 15: "Hence the beam sweeping/training complexity is B for U UEs"; Table I counts beam training time slots, which is signaling overhead. No order of complexity, FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the DRL is given.
q5_support: p. 3: "based on the publicly-available DeepMIMO dataset [28]"; p. 13: scenario O1_60 of DeepMIMO is used for learning and evaluation. The paper releases no code of its own.
notes: Included, area 3 (joint BS beamformer and RIS reflection codebook). q3 is borderline: the only learned baseline, DDPG, appears in Fig. 6 as convergence of beamforming gain over iterations (v3 rule: convergence alone does not count) and is a variant of the proposed framework; reviewer may reconsider. q4 is borderline: Table I is time-slot overhead; the hidden-layer sizes (16M and 32M neurons, p. 13) are architecture, not a stated complexity.
